# dsh-second-angle

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that gives a finished turn a second
angle: it checks the answer's claims a

gainst the tool output that turn actually read, steers a correction when the
evidence contradicts a
claim, and flags claims the evidence does not back.
Version 0.2 also checks the turn's **actions** with deterministic patterns: tool requests, exposed r

easoning and
visible text. ACTIONS makes no model calls. It reports by default, with opt-in blocking

for RED patterns before a
tool runs. The existing claim auditor remains enabled by default; set `cl

aimsEnabled: false` for an entirely
model-free check.
## Why
We tested the method on a private bench of our own sessions. The bench held one answer that used too

ls, with three
known errors and three true claims. The auditor saw it together with that turn's own

tool output. With thinking off
and a short facts-and-limits card, it flagged all three errors in 5 o

f 5 runs (five sampling seeds at temperature
0.7). Each run also flagged one true claim that the tur

n had not read. It named the right reason for the hardest
error in 5 of 5. A check took about 16 sec

onds. With short thinking on and the same card, it was about 9–11 times
slower and no more accurate.
A scan for absolute words, with no model, caught only the two errors that used one. On answers writt

en without any
tool read, an auditor that sees only evidence flagged every claim, true or false. So

the plugin feeds the auditor
the turn's own reads, keeps thinking off, puts the free scan in front,

and never sends a turn without reads to the
model.
## Install
The plugin is a harness bundle (`"dsh": { "bundle": … }` in `package.json`). Install it into a profi

le. The examples
use the shipped `headless` profile, which runs one task from the command line; anot

her profile name gets the base
layers and the plugin only. If you run the harness through `npx @deep

seek-ai/dsh`, type that in place of `dsh`.
`dsh plugin` uses the pnpm on your PATH.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A git install builds the plugin with its `prepare` script (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`, which write

s `lib/`), and
pnpm runs that only after you allow it: the first `add` stops with `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_

PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED` and prints
the key to add under `allowBuilds` in the profile's `pnpm-workspace.

yaml`. For a GitHub install the key has this
form, where `<commit>` is the full 40-character commit

itHub install the key has this
form, where `<commit>` is the full 40-character commit pnpm resolved:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
pnpm prints the key on one long line, and a terminal narrower than the line wraps it; if it breaks a

cross lines, join
the pieces with no space. A bare package name does not approve a git dependency (t

he example in the harness guide
*Installing from GitHub*
uses one). Add the key and run the same `ad

d` again. The `add` warns about peer dependencies (the running harness
provides them), and a git ins
tall first downloads the build tools (about 105 MB); the tarball needs no build.
Check the result with `dsh --profile headless --dump-config`: the tree shows a `# == dsh-second-angl

e` layer. Then
run a task with `dsh headless "<task>"`. Requires DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3

.0` (declared in `engines.dsh`).
Older 0.1.x harnesses may install the package without enforcing tha

t range, then fail to load it because required
exports are missing. Upgrade the harness before insta

l to load it because required
exports are missing. Upgrade the harness before installing the plugin.
## Configure
Every field is optional. Override them in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (in `$DSH_HOME/profiles/

<profile>/`,
`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/` by default) by restating the row (a patch replaces the row

's whole `config`). In a new
profile that file holds `[]`: replace that line with the row.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| field | default | meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | master switch |
| `claimsEnabled` | `true` | enable the original claim scanne

r/auditor; `false` leaves the free ACTIONS path |
| `actionsMode` | `flag` | `flag` reports finished
-turn action patterns; `block` also denies RED action patterns before calls (SAID-VS-DID is report-o

nly); `off` disables ACTIONS |
| `actionsAllowedHosts` | `[]` | exact remote hostnames/IPs or explic

it `*.example.org` subdomains; loopback is accepted automatically |
| `actionsToolRequirement` | `au
to` | observe explicit visible system/policy tool requirements; `required` declares an always-call r

ule supplied elsewhere by the deployment |
| `mode` | `sync` | `sync` waits for the verdict before t
he turn closes (so a contradiction can steer a correction in the same turn); `async` lets the turn c

lose at once and attaches the verdict later |
| `maxLatencyMs` | `45000` | an audit that takes longe
r is abandoned and the turn goes on (a sync turn waits at most one second more, even when a provider

ignores the abort) |
| `includeSubagents` | `false` | also publish sub-agent turn-end audits; block

-mode guards always cover every agent |
[该节后续省略]
## ACTIONS: what the turn did
The free ACTIONS check observes committed `tool/call` events and all assistant text and exposed reas

oning. It
includes nested `run_code` dispatches, requests with missing/error results, and calls made

during a steered
correction. It scans at `turn/end`, including error and abort endings. It does not
send action data to a model.
| Rule | Patterns and severity |
| **SAID-VS-DID** | An explicit English promise such as “I will not invoke any tools” followed by a
request, or a later “I did not use tools” denial. RED when the observed request conflicts with that
statement; AMBER when a visible/configured tool requirement or unattributed call makes model choice
uncertain. The matched text/reasoning is included. Scoped promises are excluded; this rule never blo

cks a call. |
| **NETWORK** | Shell network programs, cloud CLIs, HTTP/socket code one-liners, web/H
TTP tools. Explicit off-list shell/code destinations and unresolved raw-network destinations are RED
; destinations supplied only through curl/wget configuration or URL files are AMBER. Ordinary regist
ry installs and implicit git remotes are AMBER when configuration hides the actual host. DNS lookups
are AMBER. The 0.2.1-rc.2 harness `web_fetch` and `web_search` calls are AMBER for ordinary browsin

g; credential URLs, cloud metadata and off-list raw IPs are RED. |
[该节后续省略]
